text:
Alyssa: heads-up — we've gotten 3 separate bugs this week from customers using Next.js edge functions where our JS SDK blows up with `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module`. Looks like our published package still resolves the CJS entry in some bundlers. Anyone fought this recently? :thinking:

Jordan: ugh, yep. Common culprits: package.json `type` confusion + conditional `exports` that some packagers ignore. For example, we have:```json
{
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js",
      "import": "./dist/index.esm.js"
    }
  }
}```

That works for Node + bundlers that respect `exports`, but Edge runtimes (Vercel/Workers) and some older toolchains will still pick the wrong file or fail to resolve types.

Sam C: add to that: TypeScript type resolution is its own beast. Older TS versions don't consult conditional `exports` for `.d.ts` resolution reliably. If you only put type entrypoints inside `exports` it can break `tsc`/IDE users. We saw this with the auth SDK last year. Practical fixes:
- Publish a single top-level `dist/index.d.ts` and set `types` to that file (it can re-export more specific types)
- Use `typesVersions` for older TS mapping if you must support old typings resolution
- Option: ship an ESM-only companion package like `@redwood/inference-edge` for edge runtimes and keep the main package dual (CJS+ESM)

Maria: +1 to companion package for speed of iteration. Having a separate `-edge` package allows us to do stricter ESM-only builds (no CJS glue), smaller bundles for edge, and clear migrations for customers. Downside: GH maintenance and cross-version parity headaches.

Alyssa: tradeoffs exactly. Our goal is low onboarding friction for sample apps (Next.js, Cloudflare, Bun) — extra packages can confuse users. But shipping one package that silently breaks for edge is worse.

Jordan: Another idea: keep single package but publish a small entrypoint wrapper pattern: top-level `index.js` is tiny and dynamically re-exports from `./dist/node` or `./dist/edge` depending on env. But that relies on consumers executing that wrapper in the correct environment (some bundlers will inline it and still pick wrong file). Not ideal.

Sam C: code example for safe type entrypoint pattern we used before:```ts
// types/index.d.ts
export * from './node-types';
export * from './shared-types';
```
Then package.json has "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts" and `exports` can still point to runtime files. This avoids TS conditional-export pitfalls because `types` is a single resolvable path.

Maria: FYI PublishBot just posted a failed publish yesterday for 1765400000 — it was because the `prepublish` step deleted `dist/edge` inadvertently. We should add a CI check that installs the tarball and runs a tiny edge sample (like a Vercel edge worker) to catch runtime resolution errors before releasing.

PublishBot: CI run failed — integration:edge-sample (canary) — runtime import error detected on node:edge environment. See https://ci/reports/12345

Alyssa: action items I propose:
1) Short-term: Add `dist/types/index.d.ts` and set `types` to it. Publish patch canary and test with Next sample app.
2) Medium-term: prototype `@redwood/inference-edge` ESM-only package for a couple weeks and update the edge sample docs.
3) Add CI smoke: npm pack + install into edge sample (Vercel dev or wrangler dev).

Jordan: sounds good. I'll open an RFC for the companion package and a small PR for the `types` change. Sam — can you add the `typesVersions` mapping for older TS in the PR?

Sam C: yep, will add typesVersions and a quick test matrix for TS 4.6/4.9 in the CI job.

Maria: I'll own the edge smoke test and add the tarball install step to the publish pipeline.

Alyssa: great — thanks all. Let's try to keep the dual-package docs concise and add a migration note in the onboarding sample so customers don't get confused. :shipit:
